open_points.subject: A1 settling-time clock
open_points.text: its age is below the settling time, which includes a modification time in the future
open_points.question: What clock supplies the current instant used to calculate file age?
options: wall-clock time from the operating system
an injected clock shared by the whole scan
open_points.default_guess: Inject a UTC wall clock because filesystem modification times cannot be compared directly with a monotonic clock.

witness.initial: A file has a modification time close to the settling boundary and the system wall clock is adjusted during the scan.
events: The scanner reads the file modification time.
The system wall clock moves backward.
The scanner evaluates the file's age.
outcomes: A wall-clock implementation classifies the file as settling.
An implementation using a stable operation instant classifies the file as ready.
witness.observer: the caller receiving the scan status

open_points.subject: A1 settling-time representation
open_points.text: A file exactly at the settling time or exactly at the source limit passes that rule.
open_points.question: In what representation and precision are the modification time, current instant and settling duration compared, and how is equality determined after conversion?
options: timezone-aware UTC datetime values at filesystem precision
the filesystem's native timestamp representation converted with a specified rounding rule
open_points.default_guess: Compare integer Unix nanoseconds without rounding.

witness.initial: A filesystem records a modification time whose precision is coarser than the application's clock, placing the calculated age fractionally on opposite sides of two minutes depending on conversion.
events: The filesystem returns the stored modification time.
The scanner converts it and compares it with the settling duration.
outcomes: Truncation makes the file exactly old enough and it passes.
Rounding preserves an age below the boundary and it remains settling.
witness.observer: the caller receiving the scan status

open_points.subject: A1 scan clock readings
open_points.text: A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status.
open_points.question: Does one scan capture one current instant for all age checks, or read the clock separately for each file?
options: one instant captured at the start of the scan
one instant captured after directory enumeration
a fresh instant for each file
open_points.default_guess: Capture one instant at the start of the scan.

witness.initial: Two files have the same modification time and cross the settling boundary while a slow scan is running.
events: The scan starts just before both files reach the settling time.
outcomes: With one scan instant, both files are settling.
With per-file readings, the first file is settling and the second is ready.
witness.observer: the caller receiving the two observations

open_points.subject: A1 directory-listing snapshot
open_points.text: A name is judged as the directory listing returns it, and that judgement holds for the whole scan.
open_points.question: Are all directory listings captured as one scan snapshot, or is each directory listed only when traversal reaches it, allowing names created meanwhile to enter the same scan?
options: capture every directory listing at the start
list each directory when traversal reaches it
exclude every entry created after the scan-start instant even if a later listing returns it
open_points.default_guess: List each directory when traversal reaches it and judge the entries returned by that listing.

witness.initial: The photo folder contains subfolder `b`; no photo is initially inside it.
events: The scanner lists and processes an earlier subfolder `a`.
outcomes: A per-directory listing includes and reports `b/new.jpg`.
witness.observer: the caller receiving the scan results

open_points.subject: A1 listed-path replacement
open_points.text: A file renamed after the listing is no longer at the listed path, so reading it for placing fails with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
open_points.question: If the listed file is renamed but another regular file appears at the same listed path before it is opened, must placement reject the stale observation or may it read and place the replacement?
options: bind the observation to file identity and reject any replacement
bind only to the listed path and read the replacement
rehash the replacement and continue only if its content matches the observed source id
open_points.default_guess: Reject unless the opened file can be proven to be the same filesystem object that was listed.

witness.initial: `photo.jpg` is listed as an ordinary regular file.
events: Another actor renames the listed file to `old.jpg`.
The actor creates a different regular file at `photo.jpg`.
The owner requests placement of the listed observation.
outcomes: An identity-bound implementation returns `unreadable_file` and writes nothing.
A path-bound implementation reads and may place the new `photo.jpg`.
witness.observer: the owner and the binary-store operator

open_points.subject: INV-18 Required tests
open_points.text: And a file renamed to a conflict copy after the listing fails with `unreadable_file` and writes nothing (`test_a_file_renamed_to_a_conflict_copy_after_the_scan_is_not_placed`).
open_points.question: What Required tests item shows the converse case required by the listing-time judgment: a conflict-copy name returned by the listing remains ignored if it is renamed to an ordinary name during that scan?
options: add a test that renames a listed conflict copy before it would be read and proves it remains absent
state that the judgment is retained only for names accepted by the listing
remove the whole-scan persistence rule and judge the current name when opened
open_points.default_guess: Add the converse test and require the listed conflict copy to remain absent until a later scan.

witness.initial: A conflict copy exists when its directory is listed.
events: The listing returns its conflict-copy name and it is judged ignored.
The owner renames it to an ordinary photo name before traversal finishes.
outcomes: A listing-bound implementation keeps it absent for this scan.
A current-name implementation reports it as an ordinary photo in this scan.
witness.observer: the owner reading the scan results

open_points.subject: A1 renamed-file refusal
open_points.text:
A file renamed after the listing is no longer at the listed path, so reading it for placing fails
with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The refusal code must be named through its models enumeration, an imported policy constant, or a config field, as appropriate, rather than supplied as an unbound literal value.

open_points.subject: INV-18 conflict-substitution test
open_points.text: When that ordinary file disappears before it is read for placing, the conflict copy is not read in its place: the photo fails with `unreadable_file` and nothing is written (`test_a_conflict_copy_is_never_read_in_place_of_the_ordinary_file`).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The required refusal code must be named through its declared value path rather than supplied as an unbound literal value.
